query: What are the practical failure modes of transactional outbox pattern implementations in production?

facts.desc: A service cannot atomically update its DB and publish to a broker, and 2PC spanning DB+broker is not viable ('it is not viable to use a traditional distributed transaction (2PC)'); AWS frames this as the 'dual write' problem. https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transactional-outbox.html ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/cloud-design-patterns/transactional-outbox.html

Delivery is at-least-once, so consumers must be idempotent / deduplicate ('a message consumer must be idempotent, perhaps by tracking the IDs of the messages'; Debezium: consumers must 'be prepared for these at-least-once semantics and be able to detect and discard any duplicates'). https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transactional-outbox.html ; https://debezium.io/blog/2019/02/19/reliable-microservices-data-exchange-with-the-outbox-pattern/

The message relay may publish a message more than once, e.g. it crashes after publishing but before recording that fact, and republishes on restart. https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transactional-outbox.html

Ordering is preserved per aggregate by using the aggregate ID as the Kafka message key so all events for one aggregate land on the same partition in production order. https://debezium.io/blog/2019/02/19/reliable-microservices-data-exchange-with-the-outbox-pattern/

One relay implementation is transaction-log tailing / log-based CDC (e.g. Debezium): 'As opposed to any polling-based approach, event capture happens with a very low overhead in near-realtime'. https://debezium.io/blog/2019/02/19/reliable-microservices-data-exchange-with-the-outbox-pattern/ ; https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transaction-log-tailing.html

The other relay implementation is the polling publisher, which repeatedly queries the outbox table; it works with any SQL database but is 'tricky to publish events in order' and has higher overhead/latency than log tailing. https://microservices.io/patterns/data/polling-publisher.html

The outbox table grows unless rows are deleted; Debezium shows deleting events immediately so 'no separate house-keeping process is required to stop it from growing indefinitely'; AWS's relay deletes rows after successful publish. https://debezium.io/blog/2019/02/19/reliable-microservices-data-exchange-with-the-outbox-pattern/ ; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/cloud-design-patterns/transactional-outbox.html

Application-level failure mode: the pattern is 'potentially error prone since the developer might forget to publish the message/event after updating the database'. https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transactional-outbox.html

traps.desc: False: the outbox pattern gives at-least-once delivery, not exactly-once end-to-end; duplicates are expected and consumers must deduplicate (microservices.io, Debezium blog). Inflected verb forms avoid matching negations like 'does not guarantee exactly-once delivery'.

False: the whole point of the pattern is to AVOID 2PC/XA ('2PC is not used' — microservices.io). Requires 'outbox pattern' as immediate subject so correct sentences like 'without the outbox, atomicity requires 2PC' don't match.
False: the pattern creates the need for consumer idempotency (the relay can republish), it does not remove it. Inflected-form regex does not match 'does not eliminate'.
False: ordering is only preserved per aggregate/partition (aggregate-ID keying — Debezium blog); there is no global/total order across all aggregates.

False mechanism claim: Debezium does not poll the outbox table; it performs log-based CDC tailing the transaction log (WAL/binlog), which is why the table can stay empty. https://debezium.io/blog/2019/02/19/reliable-microservices-data-exchange-with-the-outbox-pattern/

contested.topic: relay mechanism: polling vs log tailing
contested.desc: microservices.io lists both as valid Message Relay implementations: polling is simple and portable but tricky to order and adds load/latency (https://microservices.io/patterns/data/polling-publisher.html); log tailing/CDC is low-overhead near-realtime but database-specific and 'tricky to avoid duplicate publishing' (https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transaction-log-tailing.html).

Position A (CDC-based): delete events immediately after insert — the table stays effectively empty (https://debezium.io/blog/2019/02/19/reliable-microservices-data-exchange-with-the-outbox-pattern/). Position B (polling-based): rows are retained until the broker acknowledges publication, then deleted by cleanup/retention jobs (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/cloud-design-patterns/transactional-outbox.html).

contested.topic: outbox vs event sourcing as the solution
contested.desc: microservices.io explicitly lists Event Sourcing as 'an alternative solution' to the same atomic update-and-publish problem, while the outbox keeps a conventional domain model (https://microservices.io/patterns/data/transactional-outbox.html).
